sentences.text: This ancient bird possessed a wingspan reaching approximately six meters, or twenty feet, ranking it among the largest avians in history.
Scientists described Gigantornis eaglesomei based on a fragmentary fossil discovered within the Middle Eocene Ameki Formation in Nigeria.
The sole known specimen is a damaged breastbone recovered from this specific geological layer.
The breastbone featured a short, deep crest, a structure common in birds that rely on dynamic soaring.
Originally grouped with albatrosses, this creature is now assigned to the pseudotooth bird family Pelagornithidae.
It inhabited the region between forty-eight point zero seven and thirty-seven point seven one million years ago.
Researchers argue whether Gigantornis represents a unique genus or if it is actually the same species as Dasornis emuinus.
